newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Default exposes regulatory snags at Karachi bourse.
newsitem.headline: Default exposes regulatory snags at Karachi bourse.

text.p: This week's eviction of a defaulting broker has sent shivers through the Karachi Stock Exchange (KSE), although the KSE says claims of 60 million rupees ($1.48 million) against the firm involved are covered.
The KSE suspended the membership of M. Rashid Jamal's MRJ Securities for failing to pay money owed in share transactions and to deliver sold shares on Tuesday's settlement day.
It said on Wednesday it would auction MRJ Securities' trading card and the company's other assets at the exchange and use the proceeds to help cover outstanding claims.
A research note by brokerage house Taurus Securities said the default had exposed crucial underlying regulatory problems at the Karachi stock exchange, Pakistan's biggest bourse.

"Apart from the immediate problem of settling MRJ's outstanding trades, this latest crisis throws up fundamental questions regarding the ability of the exchange to regulate itself and the role of the government regulatory body, the Corporate Law Authority (CLA)," Taurus Securities said.
KSE President Arif Habib said claims totalling 60 million rupees against Rashid Jamal were comprehensively covered.
"There is nothing to worry for those who had made deals through the Stock Exchange. The KSE is responsible to look after investors' interest," he told Reuters.
"If there is any shortfall in raising the money for the registered claims by selling MRJ's membership card and assets, it would be paid through KSE's protection fund," Habib said.
The KSE has a clearing house protection fund that has a limit of 12.5 million rupees to bridge any shortfall in meeting the registered claims of a defaulting member.
It is the second time this year that a KSE member has failed to honour deals with his clients. On February 28, the KSE suspended the membership of broker Yusuf Ismail Nagaria.
A senior broker, who asked not to be identified, said MRJ Securities' losses had arisen from short-selling shares in Pakistan Telecommunication Company Ltd (PTCL) PTCA.KA.
"MRJ kept selling short when the stock was rising... a gamble which ruined the company," he said.
He said several brokers had suffered losses on unregistered deals with MRJ in the kerb market, for which the KSE was not responsible.
"It is also a matter of concern for the market, but few will acknowledge it as those deals were unregistered."
Taurus Securities said the KSE had an unblemished record of meeting its liabilities under the clearing house system.
"All previous member defaults to the House have been swiftly settled through asset sales. However, its ability to do so rests on limiting potential defaults to manageable levels," it said.
Haji Ghani Haji, a senior member at the KSE, said the exchange had cut the exposure limit of members to 60 million rupees from 80 million following the MRJ case.
"The default is the result of speculative trading. The KSE was over-confident that there would be no default," he said. "Now there is a need to examine the issue."

Nasir Shah Bukhari of brokers KASB & Co said short-selling was legally outlawed, but KSE practices favoured this mode of trading. "When carry-forward deals are done, it encourages speculators to sell short," he said.
He said the KSE had an built-in mechanism to check defaults, but should now crack down on short-selling.
"Short-selling depresses the market in an artificial way and hurts the interest of genuine investors," he declared.
Bukhari said major brokerage houses played safe and stayed out of trouble, but added that other speculators could run into difficulty given prevailing trading practices.

The Corporate Law Authority last week formed a committee to examine the issue of short-selling. KSE members say that after MRJ's fall from grace, the committee should review the KSE's regulatory system and propose trading reforms.
"This latest incident must prompt both the KSE and the CLA to undertake a major review of the supervisory and regulatory mechanism for the exchange," Taurus Securities said.
